claims.claim: The Visit Wizard guides clinicians through 17 sections — from consent to provider attestation — and produces billing codes for review before the note is signed.

claims.claim: When opened, the wizard is tied to the selected patient and appointment.
Mark as Complete — finish each section with Mark as Complete. In the section navigator, completed sections are green with a checkmark, and sections that still need documentation or review are red.

checks.note: a section navigator would have to exist

claims.finding: There is no section navigator: each section's accordion header carries a status icon (StatusIcon, VisitWizardV4.tsx:11261-11301 at v1.1.345). Complete = green check; missing required items = red warning (validation re-runs on every change, :6063-6065); flagged for review = yellow warning; otherwise a grey circle. Sections needing review are yellow, not red, and untouched sections are grey.
claims.proposed_text: Mark as Complete — finish each section with Mark as Complete. Each section's header shows its status: a green checkmark when it is complete, a red warning when required items are missing, a yellow warning when it is flagged for review, and a grey circle otherwise.

claims.claim: Continuous autosave — each field is saved as you complete it, so drafts survive network drops and device switches. The web app is online-only.
Warnings, not blocks — most missing items raise a warning and let you continue. Before signing, a final review lists open gaps so you can resolve them or continue anyway.
Carry-forward — information from earlier visits carries into sections such as Review of Systems.

Per-wound documentation — interventions, care plans, procedures, and billing are documented separately for each active wound.
LCD support — the LCD Navigator tracks Medicare LCD documentation requirements as you work, and Section 16 shows any remaining gaps.

Drafting help — Summarize prior treatments, Generate Procedure Note, Generate Draft (care plan), and Generate Compliance Note create starting text from what you documented; you can keep your own procedure wording with Use My Exact Procedure Note.

claims.claim: The 17 sections are numbered 1 Consent & Attestation, 2 Patient Context, 2B Clinical History Review, 3 Review of Systems, 4 Objective Assessment, 5 Functional Status & ADLs, 6 Comorbidities & Risk Factors, 7 Wound Assessment, 8 Previous Treatments, 9 Interventions & Treatments, 10 Care Planning, 11 Orders & DME, 12 Patient Education, 13 (procedures and supplies), 14 Current Medication, 15 Billing & Documentation, 16 LCD Audit & Review, 17 Provider Attestation.
claims.reason: Badge order verified by reading VisitWizardV4.tsx:16976-18686 at v1.1.345 (Step 1 … Step 17, with Step 2b after Step 2). Section titles that differ from the page are separate claims (ov-19, ov-29).

claims.claim: Section 1 Consent & Attestation: patient consent by electronic signature, signed paper consent, or verbal consent. Consent can also be collected beforehand from the patient chart.
Section 2 is titled Patient Context / Demographics.
claims.finding: The section header reads 'Patient Context & Demographics' (VisitWizardV4.tsx:17043 at v1.1.345).

claims.claim: Section 2 covers visit type, chief complaint, and insurance (read-only here — edit it on the Insurance tab).

the section would have to point to an Insurance tab

claims.finding: Section 2 has Service Date, Place of Service, Clinician Provider, Supervising Provider, Supervision Method, Home Health Agency, Facility, Chief Complaint, Running HPI and view-only insurance (PatientDemographicsVisit.tsx:901-1612 at v1.1.345). There is no visit-type field. The insurance tooltips say 'Edit it on the patient's Billing & Auth page' (:1571, :1598, :1607); there is no Insurance tab.
claims.proposed_text: Date and place of service, clinician and supervising provider, facility, Chief Complaint and Running HPI, and insurance (view only here — edit it on the patient's Billing & Auth page).

claims.claim: Section 2B Clinical History Review: allergies and medical history.
Section 3 Review of Systems: body-system review; carries forward from earlier visits.
Section 4 Objective Assessment: vitals, vascular and perfusion exam, edema and circumference measurements, ABI/TBI, vascular studies, HbA1c, vascular follow-up plan.
Section 5 Functional Status & ADLs: mobility, daily activities, fall risk.
claims.finding: The section has Current Mobility Level and the ADL assessment (WoundCaseFunctionalStatusVisit.tsx at v1.1.345); no fall-risk field exists anywhere in the visit wizard (no 'fall risk' or 'Morse' under frontend/src/components/visit-wizard or VisitWizardV4.tsx).
claims.proposed_text: Mobility level and activities of daily living (ADLs).

claims.claim: Section 6 Comorbidities & Risk Factors: conditions that contribute to the wound or slow healing.
Section 7 Wound Assessment: etiology, staging, dimensions, tissue percentages, location, exudate, pain, infection signs, photos, and Treating / Monitoring status.
Section 8 Previous Treatments: prior wound care, chronicity, medical necessity statement, supporting documents.

checks.note: a chronicity field would have to exist in the section

claims.finding: Previous Treatments records each prior treatment (name, Treatment Dates, Duration (weeks), Outcome, Source), the Medical Necessity Statement and Supporting Documents (PreviousTreatmentsVisit.tsx:1579-2404 at v1.1.345). There is no chronicity field; wound age is computed from the onset date only to seed the draft text (:519-529).
claims.proposed_text: Prior wound care (each treatment with dates, duration and outcome), the per-wound medical necessity statement, and supporting documents.

claims.claim: Section 9 Interventions & Treatments: interventions performed per wound, procedure note, contributing factors. Section 10 Care Planning: per-wound follow-up interval, next visit date, treatment plan narrative.

checks.pattern: placeholder="Additional treatment plan details and notes..."

claims.claim: Section 13 is titled Procedures & Supplies.
claims.finding: The Step 13 header reads 'Procedure Supplies' (VisitWizardV4.tsx:18355 at v1.1.345).

claims.claim: Section 11 Orders & DME: DME, labs, imaging, referrals, and home health orders, sent by fax or email.
Section 12 Patient Education: education library, care bundles, topics covered, patient understanding, next-visit goals.
Section 13: final review of the procedures from Section 9, missing fields, procedure and compliance notes, supplies.
Section 14 Current Medication: active prescriptions, medication status, allergies, reconciliation, DoseSpot e-prescribing.
Section 15 Billing & Documentation: per-wound and visit-level codes, modifiers, and the CMS-1500 claim preview.
Section 16 LCD Audit & Review: documentation gaps against the applicable LCD.
Section 17 Provider Attestation covers attestation, E/M time, final review, progress note preview, and Sign & Lock.

checks.note: the final review / Sign & Lock would have to be reached from inside step 17

claims.finding: Step 17 holds the attestation, NPI/title, Total E/M time and Complete Provider Attestation (ProviderAttestationVisit.tsx:644-818 at v1.1.345). The final review, note preview and Sign & Lock start from the Continue to Review button in the wizard footer, outside Step 17 (VisitWizardV4.tsx:19062-19086 inside WizardLayoutFooter; preview :16532; MultiWoundReviewModal :19187).
claims.proposed_text: Attestation and E/M time. Then Continue to Review, at the bottom of the wizard, runs the final review, shows the progress note preview, and opens Sign & Lock.

claims.claim: Can I customize the charting? Not per practice. The Visit Wizard's sections, fields, and templates are the same for every organization.

checks.note: a per-facility switch that hides a section would contradict 'the same for every organization'

claims.finding: One per-facility setting changes the wizard: when facility.captures_vitals_on_followup is false, Objective Assessment (Step 4) renders nothing on follow-up visits (VitalsAssessmentVisit.tsx:3935-3940, useFacilityConfig.ts:30 at v1.1.345). No screen sets it (the column is read only by useFacilityConfig), so a practice cannot change it itself.
claims.proposed_text: Not by your practice. There is no screen to change the Visit Wizard's sections, fields, or templates, and they are the same for every organization, with one exception: Medipyxis can turn off Objective Assessment on follow-up visits for a facility.

claims.claim: If your practice needs a field or a change, send the request to your Medipyxis contact; requests are reviewed and changes that fit can be added for everyone.

The Visit Wizard saves continuously, so you rarely need to save manually. A visit you leave before Sign & Lock stays an unsigned draft that you can resume on any device. To stop a visit you won't finish, cancel or delete the appointment.
Always review carried-forward and pulled values — they are a starting point, not a substitute for re-assessment.
Section 17 records the provider's attestation and electronic signature. After a final review and a preview of the progress note PDF, Sign & Lock finalizes the note.
Later changes require an Addendum with a documented reason.

claims.claim: CMS requires that the rendering provider be physically present at the place of service for in-person procedure codes. The encounter record is part of the audit trail and may be requested during a Medicare audit.
The web Visit Wizard is online-only and saves continuously to the server.
